bull_bear.body:
- distribution: hub-and-spoke network concentrating advanced embryology and laboratory capabilities at hub centres while spokes extend geographic reach — evidence: 7 hubs and 28 spokes across more than 30 locations as at March 31, 2026
- technology: AI-assisted embryology tools (SiD and ERICA) and the GAAT platform support process standardisation and consistency of clinical outcomes across the network — evidence: SiD evaluates sperm parameters and ERICA ranks embryo viability across 2.5 million parameters, integrated into routine clinical practice from April 1, 2026 — against it: the tools were integrated after FY26 year-end (April 2026), so the FY26 results do not reflect their impact
- integration: bundled care pathway combining IVF/ART with hospital and pharmacy services within the same patient journey — evidence: the Company generates revenue from associated hospital and pharmacy activities (via Gaudium International Private Limited) alongside core IVF services
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Arbitration proceedings initiated by Neomile Corporate Advisory Limited — Seeking interim reliefs inclusive of GST, with a Sole Arbitrator appointed by order dated April 02, 2026; management considers the claim baseless but flags that progress should be tracked closely given the quantum.
- Operational, medical-legal and reputational risk inherent to fertility healthcare — Includes the risk of patient complaints or medical negligence claims; the sector carries isolated patient complaints and a Delhi Medical Council advisory relating to advertising practices at an acquired entity.
- Dependence on key medical talent and on the founder-Promoters — Explicitly flagged dependence on Dr. Manika Khanna and Dr. Peeyush Khanna, and more broadly on doctors, nurses and embryologists, in a market where scarce clinical talent constrains the pace of new-centre roll-out.
- Tax litigations under appeal — Multiple assessment-year matters (Sections 133A, 271DA, 147, 143) pending before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals); management, based on expert legal opinion, expects these to be set aside with no resulting liability.
- Consumer grievance litigation — A consumer complaint before the Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission - IX (East) continues to be contested by the Company, which expects a favourable outcome.
- Interest rate risk on floating-rate borrowings — No hedging instruments are currently used against floating-rate borrowings.
- Credit risk / slowing receivables collection — Credit risk on trade receivables is managed through an expected credit loss provision matrix; the receivables turnover ratio slowed further as the network scales, per the MD&A financial-risks discussion.
- Fragmented, inconsistent state-level regulatory implementation — Inconsistent state-level interpretation and implementation of the ART (Regulation) Act and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act creates operational and compliance variability, per the SWOT weaknesses.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited provides In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), Intrauterine Insemination (IUI), fertility preservation and other Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) and women's healthcare services across India through an asset-light hub-and-spoke model, with advanced embryology laboratories concentrated at hub centres and spoke locations providing patient access for consultation, monitoring and follow-up. In addition to core IVF services, the Company generates revenue from associated hospital and pharmacy activities that capture related patient spend within the same care pathway.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **IVF/ART treatment:** In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), Intrauterine Insemination (IUI), fertility preservation, genetic testing, gynaecological care
- **Hospital:** 15-bed hospital at Janakpuri (delivery and post-natal care)
- **Pharmacy:** fertility medications, via Gaudium International Private Limited
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Gaudium International Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); conducts pharmacy operations and supplies drugs and medical consumables to the Company; also a related party under Form AOC-2.
- EKK Global Private Limited — related party: Formerly a wholly owned subsidiary; the Company disinvested its entire shareholding on August 05, 2025, pursuant to strategic restructuring; ceased to be a subsidiary from that date.
- EKK Hospitality Private Limited — related party: Entity in which Dr. Manika Khanna and Mr. Vishad Khanna hold directorships, per the directorship/committee-membership annexure.
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- distribution: hub-and-spoke network concentrating advanced embryology and laboratory capabilities at hub centres while spokes extend geographic reach — evidence: 7 hubs and 28 spokes across more than 30 locations as at March 31, 2026
- technology: AI-assisted embryology tools (SiD and ERICA) and the GAAT platform support process standardisation and consistency of clinical outcomes across the network — evidence: SiD evaluates sperm parameters and ERICA ranks embryo viability across 2.5 million parameters, integrated into routine clinical practice from April 1, 2026 — against it: the tools were integrated after FY26 year-end (April 2026), so the FY26 results do not reflect their impact
- integration: bundled care pathway combining IVF/ART with hospital and pharmacy services within the same patient journey — evidence: the Company generates revenue from associated hospital and pharmacy activities (via Gaudium International Private Limited) alongside core IVF services
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Rapid Growth Strategy: calibrated rollout of 19 new IVF hubs (10 in FY27, 8 in FY28, 1 in FY29), supported by IPO proceeds and internal accruals, to strengthen pan-India brand visibility and patient footfall
- Integration of AI-led embryology (SiD and ERICA, in partnership with UK-headquartered IVF 2.0) into routine clinical practice to standardise clinical quality across the network
- Expansion of international reach via international spokes (Paris, Nigeria, Sydney) to strengthen the medical-tourism patient funnel
- Diversification beyond pure IVF into women's healthcare via the internally funded Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow, targeted for commercialisation in FY29
- Replication of the proprietary Gaudium Signature Lab (first deployed at the South Extension, New Delhi hub) as the template at every new centre
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Under the Rapid Growth Strategy, the Company plans 19 new IVF centres across cities named in the Prospectus, phased as 10 in FY27, 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29. The first new hub, at South Extension, New Delhi, became operational on July 16, 2026, housing the proprietary Gaudium Signature Lab intended as the template for every new centre; the next two hubs, at Gurgaon and Nagpur, were due to commence operations shortly thereafter. Separately, the Board approved a Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow (outlay of approximately ₹1500.00 Lakhs / up to ₹15 Crore), with commercialisation targeted for FY 2029, to be funded internally rather than from IPO proceeds. The Company has also opened three international spokes (Paris, Nigeria, Sydney) to support its medical-tourism funnel.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural demand growth from India's underpenetrated IVF market (only ~2% of India's infertile population accesses treatment annually against an estimated 25-30 million infertile couples), a declining total fertility rate below replacement level, delayed marriage/childbearing in urban India, and rising lifestyle-related infertility
- Industry consolidation from fragmented standalone clinics toward organised, multi-centre platforms, accelerated by tightening compliance requirements under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021 and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021
- Near-term margin compression as new-hub costs are incurred ahead of the revenue they are intended to generate, as the hub roll-out moves into active execution
- Emerging international-patient and medical-tourism opportunity, given India's materially lower per-cycle cost relative to the United States
- Continued investment in AI-assisted embryology tools (SiD, ERICA) and the GAAT platform positioned as a differentiator against both larger, less specialised hospital chains and smaller standalone clinics
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Gaudium IVF is a specialist, pure-play fertility-care platform operating a hub-and-spoke network of assisted reproduction centres across India, with 7 hubs and 28 spokes across more than 30 locations as at March 31, 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited provides In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), Intrauterine Insemination (IUI), fertility preservation and other Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) and women's healthcare services across India through an asset-light hub-and-spoke model, with advanced embryology laboratories concentrated at hub centres and spoke locations providing patient access for consultation, monitoring and follow-up. In addition to core IVF services, the Company generates revenue from associated hospital and pharmacy activities that capture related patient spend within the same care pathway.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Gaudium International Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); conducts pharmacy operations and supplies drugs and medical consumables to the Company; also a related party under Form AOC-2.
- EKK Global Private Limited — related party: Formerly a wholly owned subsidiary; the Company disinvested its entire shareholding on August 05, 2025, pursuant to strategic restructuring; ceased to be a subsidiary from that date.
- EKK Hospitality Private Limited — related party: Entity in which Dr. Manika Khanna and Mr. Vishad Khanna hold directorships, per the directorship/committee-membership annexure.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **IVF/ART treatment:** In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), Intrauterine Insemination (IUI), fertility preservation, genetic testing, gynaecological care
- **Hospital:** 15-bed hospital at Janakpuri (delivery and post-natal care)
- **Pharmacy:** fertility medications, via Gaudium International Private Limited

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (pan-India hub-and-spoke network across more than 30 locations)
- international patients / medical tourism (patients from over 30 countries)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural demand growth from India's underpenetrated IVF market (only ~2% of India's infertile population accesses treatment annually against an estimated 25-30 million infertile couples), a declining total fertility rate below replacement level, delayed marriage/childbearing in urban India, and rising lifestyle-related infertility
- Industry consolidation from fragmented standalone clinics toward organised, multi-centre platforms, accelerated by tightening compliance requirements under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021 and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021
- Near-term margin compression as new-hub costs are incurred ahead of the revenue they are intended to generate, as the hub roll-out moves into active execution
- Emerging international-patient and medical-tourism opportunity, given India's materially lower per-cycle cost relative to the United States
- Continued investment in AI-assisted embryology tools (SiD, ERICA) and the GAAT platform positioned as a differentiator against both larger, less specialised hospital chains and smaller standalone clinics

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Rapid Growth Strategy: calibrated rollout of 19 new IVF hubs (10 in FY27, 8 in FY28, 1 in FY29), supported by IPO proceeds and internal accruals, to strengthen pan-India brand visibility and patient footfall
- Integration of AI-led embryology (SiD and ERICA, in partnership with UK-headquartered IVF 2.0) into routine clinical practice to standardise clinical quality across the network
- Expansion of international reach via international spokes (Paris, Nigeria, Sydney) to strengthen the medical-tourism patient funnel
- Diversification beyond pure IVF into women's healthcare via the internally funded Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow, targeted for commercialisation in FY29
- Replication of the proprietary Gaudium Signature Lab (first deployed at the South Extension, New Delhi hub) as the template at every new centre

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Under the Rapid Growth Strategy, the Company plans 19 new IVF centres across cities named in the Prospectus, phased as 10 in FY27, 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29. The first new hub, at South Extension, New Delhi, became operational on July 16, 2026, housing the proprietary Gaudium Signature Lab intended as the template for every new centre; the next two hubs, at Gurgaon and Nagpur, were due to commence operations shortly thereafter. Separately, the Board approved a Gaudium Women Hospital at Lucknow (outlay of approximately ₹1500.00 Lakhs / up to ₹15 Crore), with commercialisation targeted for FY 2029, to be funded internally rather than from IPO proceeds. The Company has also opened three international spokes (Paris, Nigeria, Sydney) to support its medical-tourism funnel.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- distribution: hub-and-spoke network concentrating advanced embryology and laboratory capabilities at hub centres while spokes extend geographic reach — evidence: 7 hubs and 28 spokes across more than 30 locations as at March 31, 2026
- technology: AI-assisted embryology tools (SiD and ERICA) and the GAAT platform support process standardisation and consistency of clinical outcomes across the network — evidence: SiD evaluates sperm parameters and ERICA ranks embryo viability across 2.5 million parameters, integrated into routine clinical practice from April 1, 2026 — against it: the tools were integrated after FY26 year-end (April 2026), so the FY26 results do not reflect their impact
- integration: bundled care pathway combining IVF/ART with hospital and pharmacy services within the same patient journey — evidence: the Company generates revenue from associated hospital and pharmacy activities (via Gaudium International Private Limited) alongside core IVF services

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Arbitration proceedings initiated by Neomile Corporate Advisory Limited — Seeking interim reliefs inclusive of GST, with a Sole Arbitrator appointed by order dated April 02, 2026; management considers the claim baseless but flags that progress should be tracked closely given the quantum.
- Operational, medical-legal and reputational risk inherent to fertility healthcare — Includes the risk of patient complaints or medical negligence claims; the sector carries isolated patient complaints and a Delhi Medical Council advisory relating to advertising practices at an acquired entity.
- Dependence on key medical talent and on the founder-Promoters — Explicitly flagged dependence on Dr. Manika Khanna and Dr. Peeyush Khanna, and more broadly on doctors, nurses and embryologists, in a market where scarce clinical talent constrains the pace of new-centre roll-out.
- Tax litigations under appeal — Multiple assessment-year matters (Sections 133A, 271DA, 147, 143) pending before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals); management, based on expert legal opinion, expects these to be set aside with no resulting liability.
- Consumer grievance litigation — A consumer complaint before the Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission - IX (East) continues to be contested by the Company, which expects a favourable outcome.
- Interest rate risk on floating-rate borrowings — No hedging instruments are currently used against floating-rate borrowings.
- Credit risk / slowing receivables collection — Credit risk on trade receivables is managed through an expected credit loss provision matrix; the receivables turnover ratio slowed further as the network scales, per the MD&A financial-risks discussion.
- Fragmented, inconsistent state-level regulatory implementation — Inconsistent state-level interpretation and implementation of the ART (Regulation) Act and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act creates operational and compliance variability, per the SWOT weaknesses.

- Expansion of international reach via international spokes (Paris, Nigeria, Sydney) to strengthen the medical-tourism patient funnel

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
